definition: what I did at the break instead of going home, and what that phone call left me

settled:
The break did not end my mission, though I think many would have gone home. I got in touch with the mission president's wife, who coordinated health issues, and she connected me by phone to a church psychologist in Germany. He had me take a stress assessment and I scored at the 99th percentile. I literally could not have scored higher.

I did not view leaving as a real option, so I went back to my belief that the only way out is through. I think that traced to my deeper beliefs at the time that my needs were not important and that I always had to meet the expectations of others.

He taught me the main systems of the body, how they integrate with the autonomic nervous system, and that breathing is the semi-voluntary bridge into it. That call, at twenty, when I could not leave the room, seeded the breathing practice that anchors hours of every day now.

Three months in the training centre plus six in the field is the nine I overrode.
